summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Discussed remaining network blockers, routing (VPC peering vs transit), upgrade window for runtime kernel and inference engine, and a perf benchmark schedule. Security raised audit log retention and KMS integration questions. Agreed next steps: share network terraform snippets, run firewall tests, schedule benchmark, and finalize compliance items.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sophie Patel (Redwood SE), Tomas Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Rajesh Nair (Acme Head of AI), Maya Lopez (Platform Engineer), Kenji Saito (Security Lead), Lena Ortiz (Infra Eng)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I think we have all the regulars. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Rajesh: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to keep moving on the pilot.
[00:11] Sophie: Hi all, Sophie here. I want to focus today's sync on the remaining network blockers, the kernel/runtime upgrade plan, and lock in the perf window.
[00:22] Maya: Sounds good. We made some changes to the MTU and testing last night, will share logs.
[00:27] Kenji: And I have a few follow-ups on audit logs and KMS integration.

[00:35] Alex: Great. Quick agenda: 1) Network status (Maya/Lena), 2) Routing and fallback policies (Sophie), 3) Runtime upgrade timing (Sophie/Alex), 4) Security/compliance questions (Kenji), 5) Perf benchmark scheduling and next steps.

[01:00] Maya: On network — we tested the VPC peering path this morning. Egress to the Redwood private control plane is okay, but we saw intermittent packet drops when we push bursts of concurrent requests. Might be an MTU mismatch or the uplink tune. We're on 10Gbps links but the infra team is worried about burst shaping.
[01:22] Lena: Right, we are on 10Gbps between the compute cluster and the NAT gateway. If we switch to 25Gbps it will cost more and require a short maintenance window to bump the interface and update the switch configs.
[01:36] Sophie: Okay — two things to consider. One, for the pilot you can keep the 10Gbps but tweak the NIC offload and MTU so we avoid fragmentation on large token payloads. Two, Redwood's runtime can route low-latency requests through a dedicated path — but that requires the VPC peering and specific firewall ports to be open. I'll share the exact ports and IP ranges.
[01:58] Alex: Sophie, can you confirm the ports? We should put them in a Terraform snippet so Maya's team can apply them quickly.
[02:06] Sophie: Yeah — outbound TLS to 443 for control plane, and a set of ephemeral high ports for data plane connections (we'll provide the list). Also if you want to enable direct routing for KV cache prefetching we need to allow long-lived TCP connections on port 52000-52010 — that's the default but configurable.

[02:35] Maya: Hmm, long-lived TCP might be tricky because our firewall times out idle connections at 15m. We can increase that but need to validate with security.
[02:43] Kenji: We can alter the timeout, but we need to understand session behavior. Does the runtime keep idle connections open frequently?
[02:51] Sophie: The runtime prefers persistent connections for efficiency — it maintains a pool for the KV cache and batching. But we also support reconnects and exponential backoff; it's resilient. The important thing is to avoid NAT ephemeral port exhaustion and fragmenting big payloads.

[03:12] Rajesh: From product perspective, latency is primary for a subset of user flows — especially risk scoring which is time sensitive. For other batch flows cost is bigger. So routing policy that can route by route is important.
[03:25] Alex: Yep — Redwood supports policy-based routing: tag a route as low-latency and we'll use reserved capacity or dedicated path when available, otherwise fall back to hosted variants. For private you can pin model variants too.

[03:40] Lena: Can you explain the fallback? If the dedicated path is saturated does traffic go through Redwood hosted or stays on private but queued?
[03:47] Sophie: There are three options: 1) Queue locally in the private pool (with backpressure to the client), 2) Failover to a compatible quantized variant in the same private pool, or 3) Route to Redwood-hosted instance — the latter requires explicit policy and consent due to data residency. We'll document the default behavior and how to toggle.

[04:12] Maya: Data residency is a hard constraint for some flows — we need to make sure any failover to hosted is opt-in per route.
[04:18] Alex: Understood. We'll make sure defaults respect your tenancy settings.

[04:25] Sophie: Next, the runtime/kernel upgrade. We're proposing an upgrade to the inference engine (v2.8) and an OS kernel bump to include a newer NIC driver. This will reduce tail latencies by ~10-15% but requires a rolling maintenance window. For the pilot we can do a canary on 2 nodes first.
[04:46] Rajesh: What's the expected downtime?
[04:48] Sophie: Rolling upgrade is non-disruptive if you have at least 3 nodes; the canary will take 30–45 minutes, then we monitor for 24 hours before proceeding. Worst case, if you see regressions we can roll back.
[05:01] Lena: We usually require a 2-hour maintenance window to account for rollback and validation checks. Is that enough?
[05:07] Sophie: Yes, 2 hours is sufficient for the full cluster rotation. For the canary we only need 45 minutes. We'll coordinate with your windows.

[05:15] Kenji: On security — KMS and audit logs. We need clarification on whether the private control plane still pushes audit logs to Redwood or stores them locally and ships to our SIEM. Also we have HSM-backed key requirements for encryption at rest.
[05:29] Alex: Good question. For private deployments the control plane is customer-managed; audit logs can be routed to your SIEM via our log-forwarder or stored locally depending on config. For encryption, Redwood supports KMS integration with either cloud KMS or customer-managed HSM via KMIP. We'll send the integration doc.
[05:48] Kenji: And SOC 2 evidence — we have a standard set of questions on access controls, RBAC mappings, and SSO (SAML). Can you confirm SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for the console?
[05:59] Tomas: Yes, we support SAML-based SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll attach the SSO config guide and sample metadata.

[06:09] Rajesh: Also want to validate audit log retention. We need 13 months of logs for certain workflows. Can Redwood support that in private?
[06:16] Alex: Retention is configurable; we can keep logs locally for whichever retention you need. The cost is mainly storage. We'll include retention and pricing options in the follow-up.

[06:26] Maya: Back to networking — Sophie, you mentioned Terraform snippets. If we get those, we can quickly apply and test tonight. What's the expected IP range list?
[06:34] Sophie: We'll provide a CIDR block set and a small list of stable control-plane IPs plus the ephemeral range for data plane. It will be something like 54.23.x.x/29 for control, and 10.100.0.0/16 for data plane endpoints but we'll provide the exact values.

[06:51] Lena: Will those IPs be static? We need static for our firewall rules.
[06:56] Sophie: Control plane IPs are static for a deployment; data plane endpoints are ephemeral within the VPC but we give a maintained CIDR you can allow.

[07:05] Kenji: Encryption in transit — is mTLS supported between our nodes and the Redwood private runtime?
[07:11] Sophie: Yes, mutual TLS is supported for intra-cluster communications and we can provide cert rotation docs. For egress to the Redwood control plane we use TLS 1.2/1.3 and can optionally enable mTLS with client certs if required.

[07:27] Alex: Great. Let's talk about the perf benchmark. Sophie?
[07:30] Sophie: For the perf window we want to run a 25k total token run across a mixture of low-latency routes (risk scoring) and batch routes (document embedding). Ideally we do it during off-peak. Lena, what is your preferred day/time?
[07:44] Lena: We can do an evening slot — July 30th 19:00 PST works for the infra team.
[07:49] Rajesh: That works for us as well.

[07:53] Sophie: Perfect. Steps: I'll send the benchmark harness and the script; Lena will provision the extra test load and monitor NIC metrics. We'll capture latencies, p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and tail latency. We'll also test cold start vs warm cache.

[08:10] Maya: Cold start times are important — especially with GPU allocation. We saw a 1.2s cold start in an earlier run. Can that be improved?
[08:16] Sophie: Cold starts tie into your pool sizing and pre-warming policy. Redwood supports pre-warm instances and an async prefetcher for the KV cache. We'll show recommendations based on your expected QPS.

[08:28] Rajesh: One question on model quantization — we might accept a small quality hit for cost savings. Does Redwood support auto-quantization strategies per route?
[08:36] Sophie: Yes — in the platform you can specify quantization policies per route and per model. We provide quality monitors and eval hooks so you can compare outputs against golden prompts. If you accept a quantized variant as fallback, we can do A/B tests during the benchmark.

[08:54] Kenji: For the audit trail, we need traceability for any model variant used in production. Can logs include model id, quantization profile, and exact kernel version?
[09:04] Alex: Yes, the runtime emits structured metadata with each request: model id, model version, quant profile, runtime kernel hash, and node id. We can expand the fields if you need more.

[09:17] Maya: (laughs) small transcription glitch there — but good to know.

[09:20] Sophie: Also note the runtime kernel hash helps with reproducibility. During a canary we'll pin the kernel so you can easily audit.

[09:30] Rajesh: Any other blockers from Redwood side?
[09:33] Sophie: From our side, we need the firewall test results and confirmation on the maintenance window. We'll prepare the terraform snippets and the canary plan. We'll also prepare the perf harness and default route policies.

[09:45] Lena: On our side, we'll validate the MTU/NIC settings tonight and share logs. If the MTU tweak doesn't fix the bursts, we'll plan the upgrade to 25Gbps but that'll require a change request and schedule.

[09:59] Kenji: For SOC2 Qs, we'll send the formal questionnaire to Alex; please route it to your security team.

[10:06] Alex: Will do — I'll send the SOC2 checklist and the SAML/SCIM docs after the call.

[10:12] Tomas: Quick note — regarding pricing for pilot scale up, Alex, we discussed a mid-tier reserved pool if you need dedicated throughput for risk scoring. Can you include the outline in the follow-up?

[10:21] Alex: Yes, I'll include pilot pricing and an option for reserved capacity and pay-as-you-go comparisons.

[10:26] Rajesh: One more operational question — how do we handle incident alerts if a node goes down? Do you integrate with PagerDuty?

[10:33] Sophie: We provide alert hooks and can push to PagerDuty, Slack, or your monitoring stack. For private deployment you control the alert destinations. We'll add Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes as part of the deployment templates.

[10:45] Maya: Great. Anything else?

[10:48] Kenji: I want to double-check the KMS flow — when you say KMIP/HSM support, does that cover local HSM appliances behind a firewall?

[10:55] Alex: Yes, we support KMIP and can integrate with on-prem HSMs. We'll need an ops contact to coordinate certificate exchange.

[11:03] Maya: That should be Kenji. We'll put him on point.

[11:06] Sophie: Ok recap and next steps: 1) Sophie to send Terraform + network diagrams (2027-07-27), 2) Maya/Lena to run firewall/MTU tests and post logs (2027-07-29), 3) Sophie to run benchmark harness with Lena on 2027-07-30 19:00 PST, 4) Kenji to return SOC2 questions and KMS specifics (2027-08-03), 5) Alex to send pricing/canary/retention notes (2027-07-28).

[11:28] Rajesh: That aligns with our plan. Thanks everyone.
\[11:30] Alex: Thanks folks — we'll follow up with the artifacts shortly.

[11:35] Tomas: I'll also add these action items to the CRM and send the calendar invite for the benchmark window.

[11:40] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains a few minor auto-transcription artifacts (timestamps and speaker switches). References: SSO/SCIM guide link (sent post-call), Terraform snippets (pending), perf harness repo link (will be shared).
